issues.problem: The two titles name opposite hat actions for the same second party: ZH 脱帽的人 = 'the one(s) who took the hat off' (the uncovering salute), while EN 'the Men Who Kept Their Hats On' describes them staying covered. Both are true of Congress, but the headline points at different gestures.
issues.suggestion: Align one to the other: e.g. EN 'the Men Who Uncovered' (or ZH title '…与戴着帽子坐着的人').

issues.problem: The quoted set words differ: EN has 'Sir, The United States in Congress assembled are prepared to receive your communications.' while the ZH quotation ('合众国国会已准备好听取您的陈述。') drops the form of address 'Sir'.
issues.suggestion: Add the address to the ZH quote: '阁下，合众国国会已准备好听取您的陈述。'

issues.problem: ZH says the silence was declared by the secretary ('必要时由秘书宣布肃静'); EN leaves the actor out ('silence was to be ordered if necessary').
issues.suggestion: EN: 'silence was to be ordered by the secretary if necessary.'

issues.problem: Hedge mismatch: ZH asserts the alternatives could work '甚至更快' (even faster), while EN softens this to 'perhaps faster', adding an uncertainty absent in Chinese.
issues.suggestion: EN: change 'perhaps faster' to 'and even faster' (or ZH: '甚至更快' → '也许更快').

overall: The English edition tracks the Chinese closely in facts, dates, names, quotations and attributions; only the quoted 'Sir', the secretary-ordering-silence detail, one hedge, and the title's hat gesture need alignment.
